newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler denies Schrempp resignation threat.
newsitem.headline: Daimler denies Schrempp resignation threat.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG on Saturday denied a report that its chairman Juergen Schrempp had threatened to resign in order to force through a management restructure at the German industrial giant.

The Spiegel magazine will report in next week's edition that Schrempp warned senior officials that he would leave if they refused to accept a reshuffle that would reduce the authority of Mercedes-Benz chief Helmut Werner.
A summary of the article was released in advance.
Daimler spokesman Roland Klein described the report as "nonsense".
"This is not about individuals, it is a question of a decision about more efficient structures," Klein said of Schrempp's plans to streamline management structures.

Industry sources last week said there was a struggle to keep Werner at Mercedes following reports that he planned to resign and that Schrempp had even offered Werner the post of chairman of the restructured Daimler to persuade him to stay.
Werner has opposed a plan by Schrempp to more closely integrate the profitable Mercedes car and truck operation.
